recipes.name: Sherry Apple Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 3 large apples - peeled, cored and sliced

steps.text: In a large skillet, brown chops, about 2 minutes each side; reserve.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Arrange apple slices in the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish. Sprinkle with brown sugar and cinnamon. Dot with butter or margarine. Top with browned pork chops and season with salt and pepper to taste. Pour sherry over all, cover and bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour or until tender and the internal temperature has reached 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Sherry Apple Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Imagine pork chops resting on a bed of sliced apples dotted with butter and dusted with brown sugar and cinnamon. Then imagine sherry poured over the top. Bake until tender. Eat until satisfied.

review.reviewBody: I have never come back to write a review the same night I make a recipe, but I had to -- this was INCREDIBLY DELICIOUS! Just used some suggestions from other reviews, 4 apples, doubled br. sugar, cinnamon & butter & last 10 mins. added a 1/4 more of sherry mixed with 2T. corn starch & perfecto! I will make this again & again. Thank you!

Didn't want any leftovers so I used 2-8oz. boneless sirloin pork chops (one inch thick). Sliced but didn't peel 2 Gala apples (no seeds) and layered them in the bottom of a sprayed 8" casserole. Sprinkled generously with brown sugar and lots of cinnamon. Placed browned pork chops on top with salt and pepper. Covered. Cooked 1 hour at 350 with a sweet potato on the side. Served with "Grillin' Beans". Perfecto!

After reading several reviews I made some changes. First I marinated the chops in some Trader Joe's spiced cider and soy sauce. I salt and peppered them on both sides and browned them in butter. Next I removed the chops from the pan and sautéed the apples in a little more butter, then sprinkled brown sugar and cinnamon over and cooked until the sugar melted. I put the chops on the bottom and apples on top and sprinkled the whole thing with Captain Morgan's rum, since I had no sherry. I baked it for 35 minutes, then removed the food and thickened sauce with corn starch. My husband is still raving about this. He wants me to have a dinner party to show it off!

The flavors are perfect. I used a 2 lb pork loin that I cut into medallions and seared on medium high heat after seasoning with salt and pepper. I transferred them to a casserole dish and focused on the sauce. I added 1 tsp of cinnamon, 1/2 cup of brown sugar, 3 T of butter and 2/3 cup of sherry to deglaze the pan. I placed the apples in a casserole dish, added the pork medallions and then the sauce. I covered the dish and baked for 1 hour. I transferred the drippings to a saucepan and added 3 T of corn starch to 1/2 cup of drippings and then added it to the remainder in the pan on medium heat. The gravy was used for a topping on the pork medallions and apples along with the mashed potatoes side dish. I served petite peas and my husband and I thoroughly enjoyed this dish. Well done!

I browned two boneless pork chops in cast iron pan, pushed them to one side, then in same pan I made two stacks of sliced Granny Smith apples, topped with the brown sugar, cinnamon, butter and the pork chops and added 1/2 C Sherry. Then placed the pan in the oven for only 30 minutes. Even though this amount of sauce is the recommended amount for 6 pork chops, we used the entire amount for our two pork chops because the sauce was so delicious. This is a KEEPER!!!

ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS. I followed Gina B. Cookin's advice and doubled the butter, brown sugar and cinnamon, which I combined together and dropped in clumps onto four sliced apples which were cut onto the bottom of my baking dish (I also sprinkled dried cranberries on top of the apples, about 1/2 cup). I browned my pork chops in coconut oil and sprinkled s&p on them,then placed them on top of the apples & cranberries and brown sugar mixture. I poured the sherry over all, covered and baked for 45 minutes. Then I removed the foil and broiled on high for 10 minutes. I combined a little more than 1/4 cup of sherry with 2 T cornstarch and poured it here and there in the sauce in the pan and stirred to thicken the sauce. The apples were not mushy and there was a good amount of sauce which I also used to top mashed potatoes.

It produced far too much juice and I reduced it to a thick sauce. The sherry was a good addition though. Try adding 1 cup dry sherry with 1/2 cup water to your roasting pan when cooking your turkey. Makes for fabulous tasting pan drippings! I seared the pork chops in olive oil and butter for several minutes. I then sautéed the apple slices with cinnamon in the pan juices with finally de-glazing the pan with the sherry. Then poured all into an oven safe dish and baked as directed and covered. I do think the cover can be removed at mid-point and basting and I don't think they required an hour to cook through. Mine were perfectly fine after 45 minutes of baking.

I had to make a couple changes. Mainly, I upped the brown sugar and cinnamon and apples because I had 6 chops. I also used apple juice instead of sherry because - well, my family made me! I cooked it in a large cast iron skillet, then cooked the apples and sugar and placed chops on top followed by apple juice. I followed another reviewer and added two teaspoons of corn starch for the last ten minutes. This recipe was soooo delish! Even husband and kiddo who don't like cooked fruit in food loved it. By the way, I'm sure that the original recipe is also wonderful - I just had to appease my family. This recipe was a lot of fun to cook - perfect challenge for us newer cooks. Thanks for posting!

I threw the brown sugar, cinnamon, butter and sherry in the cast iron skillet AFTER I browned the chops to grab those little bits in the bottom of the pan. The sauce seemed thin to me, so I threw in another quarter cup of brown sugar and a couple more healthy pats of butter. The end result was fantastic. Next time, I'd use another apple or two because we were fighting over the apples that were left and there weren't any to go in the foil with the last remaining pork chop and I'd also double the cinnamon.

This rocks! I did add my own touch, which is why I will give it 4 stars... first, I seasoned the chops very well with salt and pepper. I seared them until good and brown in EVOO/butter. Then I tossed in the apples and some thinly sliced onion. I sprinkled the brown sugar and cinnamon on top and splashed the sherry over the whole thing. A little extra pinch of salt and pepper and I covered this and let it all simmer on the stove top, about 15 more min. At the very end, I added a little corn starch slurry to thicken the juices. My hubby and I devoured our chops and were picking at the remaining apples that were left in the pan... perfectly sweet and savory.

This is a wonderful recipe. I see some people mentioning a missing WOW factor and the pork chops drying out. I add a few cloves, a little nutmeg and allspice (just a little), and onions. And if you want moist pork, I highly recommend using a tenderloin or pork butt roast instead of chops. I salt and pepper the roast, then I rub it with brown sugar. If I have time, I brown on all sides in a frying pan then put it in the roasting pan on top of the apples, onions and spices and sherry (sometimes I add a little apple juice too) and roast it according to the recipe. I serve it with mashed potatoes because the sherry sauce makes a nice gravy. I think I'm going to make it for Christmas.
This is my go to pork chop recipe. Absolutely delicious 😋

This was easy enough to do. I first layered sliced sweet potatoes and onions under the apple slices to have a whole meal ready and added extra sherry. The taste was disappointing in the sense that there was not enough of the sherry taste and it was more watery then sauce like. My fault for adding extra. Wondering if perhaps doing it stove top and then using a thickening agent might have been better. I did, however, like the addition of the sweet potatoes and onions.

Great flavor! I used tawny port wine because that is listed online as a substitute for cooking sherry. My inch-thick, boneless, pork-loin chops were done (145 degree center) 40 minutes into the cooking time. I served this with roasted carrot soup and oven-baked French fries, so we did not get to take advantage of the abundant pan juices, which would have been delicious over rice.
So simple to put together and delicious. I love the sauce it makes! A bite of cooked apple with a bite of chop, YUM! My 3 sons liked it too. I will make it again.
My husband and I love this dish. It's the best recipe that I have tried from this site so far.
I've made many pork/ Apple and fruit dishes. I think this is the best of all. No changes. Could possible use a bit more sherry.
Used boneless center cut pork chopes and doubled the sauce as another reviewer suggested. Made mashed potatoes as a side - wonderful!
Made this twice and family liked it a lot. I followed the recipe as written and made no changes. I will probably make again in the future.
I made this with only two pork chops, I used apple juice and one Granny Smith apple, served with mashed potatoes and carrot and peas, my wife and I both really liked it.
